You can't just drop a preference, this throws preference file read issues. Replace with pref_register_obsolete() or something like that.

Found it.  I did search for it (obviously in the wrong header), and somehow thought they were automatically detected and removed now.

I wasn't the original author - I only just realised that the names of the items in the preference file are needlessly prefixed with "oran.".  Guess I'll need to live with that..
If this preference is only in 3.5 it ought to be ok to drop it? As It's never been released.

README.dissector 2.6 User Preferences mentions prefs_register_obsolete_preference() but doesn't say anything about if it ought to be used in this case.

I am happy to leave the call in.  I think there are a a few users of the dissector now, using master. FWIW, I didn't get any warnings in my (linux) console when I first ran Wireshark again after removing the preference.
Personally I think obsolete preferences is overengineering things...saving the preferences once gets rid of the printout. But no strong opinion either way.
Think I will leave it in, since I already added it.  I have seen the printout, but not in a long time.
